title: Nora registers the old map collection (paraphrase)
topic: A librarian named Nora catalogues a collection of old maps in the city library; a colleague brings a box from the cellar, a student asks for a river map, Nora locks the archive at six
tail_E: To make out the small place names she reaches for her magnifying
target_note: Same target as formulation A: 'glass' is the near-obligatory completion of 'reaches for her magnifying' in the old-maps context; it does not occur in the units or the tail, nor does its German equivalent (Glas / Lupe). ' glass' is a single Pythia token (id 5253); Pythia-160m ranks it first after the all-English context (p ~ 0.91).
author: LS-NEQ stimulus authoring, paraphrase of family F09
notes: Formulation B: independent re-phrasing of the ten F09A meaning units in both languages (same events, same order, same names Nora and Bremen). Replacements include catalogues in the city library/registers at the town library (katalogisiert in der Stadtbibliothek/erfasst in der Bücherei der Stadt), oldest map shows the harbour in fine lines/oldest chart depicts the port in delicate strokes (Karte zeigt den Hafen von Bremen/Seekarte zeigt den Bremer Hafen, feine Linien/zarte Striche), colleague brings a box from the cellar/co-worker carries a crate from the basement (Kollege bringt Holzkiste/Mitarbeiter trägt hölzerne Kiste), writes a number on every sheet/puts a number on each of the sheets (schreibt/setzt), paper smells of dust and salt/a smell of salt comes from the dusty sheets (subject changed to the smell: riecht/kommt), colours fade at the edges/colours grow pale along the margins (verblassen/werden blass), asks for a river map/wants a river chart (bittet um eine Flusskarte/möchte eine Karte des Flusses), notes the year in the catalogue/records the year in the register (notiert im Katalog/vermerkt im Verzeichnis), shelves reach up to the ceiling/bookshelves rise right up to the ceiling (Regale reichen/Bücherregale ragen), locks the archive at six o'clock/closes the archive at six in the evening (verschließt/schließt). No separable verbs are used. Present tense and positive polarity throughout.
